title: Cross-environment model routing mismatch causing ambiguous 5xx and client retry amplification
creator: Arianna Kim
description: Several enterprise customers reported a spike of ambiguous 5xx errors and timeouts across Hosted and Dedicated endpoints after a partial canary rollout of a new model catalog mapping. Symptoms: clients received non-deterministic HTTP 502/503 with different response bodies; some SDKs treated the responses as transient and retried aggressively, which amplified load and caused KV-cache eviction storms and tokenization mismatches on Dedicated nodes. Private (VPC) customers were affected only if they had enabled control-plane routing sync. Root cause hypothesis: control-plane routing table contained stale model variant IDs for a small subset of regions, causing requests for model-vX to be routed to model-vY (different tokenizer/architecture). The serving process returned a proto/decode error that our edge layer normalized to an opaque 502, which the SDK interpreted as retryable. The retry pattern created request amplification that saturated per-GPU queues and evicted hot KV entries, producing long tail latency and further 5xxs.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy a seeded routing table with mismatched variant ids for region eu-west-2 (test harness provided in linked doc)
Send 50 concurrent streaming generation requests using the official JS SDK with default retry settings
Observe a mix of 502/503 responses at the edge, and tail latencies on dedicated pods > 5s
Enable SDK exponential-backoff toggle and re-run to verify reduced amplification (control test)
work_done: 2026-03-12 09:40 - Triage call with oncall, PM, and customer success. Confirmed scope covers 3 customers and both hosted + dedicated pools.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Correlation: edge proto-decode errors precede 502 responses. Captured traces linked in artifacts.

2026-03-12 13:30 - Temporary mitigation: edge now differentiates decode-vs-capacity failures; decode errors are returned with 4xx mapped code and stable body to avoid client retries (hotpatch applied to edge, PR: github.com/redwood/edge/pull/8421).
2026-03-13 08:20 - Rollback of canary routing-table entries in eu-west-2 completed. Customer-visible errors dropped by ~70% within 15 minutes (dashboard: grafana.company/incident/318272).

2026-03-13 14:00 - Implemented SDK header 'X-Redwood-Routing-Version' to surface routing mismatch and enable server-side reject path for mismatched variants (prototype PR: github.com/redwood/sdk-js/pull/1290).
2026-03-14 10:10 - Runbook updated with a new 'routing-sanity' check that runs before canary promotion (Confluence: confluence.company/pages/RED-Route-Sanity).

2026-03-15 09:00 - Eng review: decided to implement a control-plane checksum and a lightweight per-request reconcile check in the edge. Trade-off: added 0.5ms p99 latency cost vs much lower customer 5xx exposure. Design doc: confluence.company/pages/RED-Route-Reconcile-Design.
acceptance_criteria: Control-plane routing checksums are computed and verified by edge before accepting traffic; mismatches return a stable 409 with actionable body
SDKs receive unambiguous non-retryable error codes for variant-mismatch and expose a flag to backoff without amplifying requests
Canary promotion pipeline includes automated routing-sanity checks with synthetic workload that mirrors customer tokenization patterns

Ship SDK header handling across official clients and bump default retry policy to safer conservative mode (owners: SDK team) - target 2026-03-20
Run cross-region canary with synthetic tokenization packs and validate KV cache stability for 48h before wide rollout
